Subject: Post-incident RCA & customer action plan — Feb 9 partial outage

Sofia / Carlos,

Thank you again for your patience while we investigated the partial outage that affected a subset of hosted inference requests on Feb 9. Below is a concise customer-facing summary, the timeline of events, and the concrete actions we're taking to prevent recurrence. We recognize the disruption this caused for Finova's production workflow and want to be fully transparent.

Summary (TL;DR)
- Incident window: 2026-02-09 22:48 UTC — 2026-02-09 23:34 UTC (approx).
- Impact: ~6% of redirected token-generation requests experienced elevated 5xx errors and increased latency; no authenticated customer data was accessed or exfiltrated.
- Root cause (short): a memory leak triggered by an edge-case in cache eviction logic under high concurrent prefix-caching load, which exhausted available GPU memory on a small number of nodes and caused cascading degraded routing decisions.

Customer-facing RCA (high-level)
1) Trigger: An uncommon request pattern from several high-concurrency jobs caused our KV prefix cache to repeatedly allocate without releasing under a race condition in the eviction path.
2) Failure mode: Affected serving instances hit OOM on GPU leading to process restarts; our smart routing attempted failover, which temporarily overloaded nearby nodes and increased error rates.
3) Data exposure: No — we confirmed there was no lateral data access; customer payloads remained isolated. Full log exports are available on request.

Incident timeline (key events)
- 2026-02-09 22:48 UTC — Elevated 5xx observed by auto-alerting (SLO deviation).
- 2026-02-09 22:52 UTC — Initial mitigation: routing throttles and temporary capacity increase applied; partial relief observed.
- 2026-02-09 23:06 UTC — Root cause identified by SRE: cache eviction race condition.
- 2026-02-09 23:15 UTC — Hotfix rollout (config change to eviction path + graceful backpressure) to affected pool.
- 2026-02-09 23:34 UTC — Metrics returned to normal; no further production errors recorded.

Customer impact details
- Finova: ~0.8% of requests from your account during the window were retried by our client SDKs; we did not retry any requests on your behalf without client config. We can provide a per-request export if you would like the list of request IDs and timestamps.

Actions we have taken (completed)
- Applied hotfix to eviction logic and rolled back risky cache path changes.
- Scaled up the affected pool and tightened routing throttles to avoid overload during failover.
- Collected full forensic logs and validated there was no data leakage.

Planned actions (owners & ETA)
- SRE (Neha Kapoor): backport fix to all stable runtimes and run a 48h soak test — ETA 2026-02-14.
- Product/Runtime (Marcus Lin): add a safety limiter to prefix-cache allocations and add additional telemetry — ETA 2026-02-21.
- CS (Lauren Bishop): schedule a 30–45 min technical review with Finova to walk the RCA and confirm deliverables — suggested windows below.

Requested next steps from Finova
1) Let us know if you’d like a per-request export of impacted request IDs/timestamps.
2) Pick a preferred time for a technical review: Feb 11 (10–11am PST), Feb 12 (2–4pm PST), or Feb 15 (all day).

Attachments: 20260210_finova_rca.pdf (concise timeline + logs excerpt).

Again, we apologize for the disruption. We're treating this with high priority and will follow up with the soak-test results and confirmation once backports are complete.

Best,

Lauren Bishop
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
